keyTakeaways: Invite 6 to 12 people: Dunbar's friendship layers put about 15 people in your 'best friends' layer, and a small flat's hallway and kitchen jam above 12.
Keep real flames out of the coat room: NFPA reports 36% of US home candle fires in 2020–2024 started in a bedroom, and over half began with something burnable too close.
In Toronto, music heard inside a neighbour's home must stay under 42 dB(A) after 11 pm, so a 7–11 pm party drops the volume at 10:30 pm on both 31 October 2026 (Saturday) and 2027 (Sunday).
Run the scare corner in pairs and debrief afterwards: haunted-attraction research links fear and contact to feeling closer, with talking it over likely the key step.
Our estimate for a 6–12 guest house party is about $11–23 a head in US dollars, with food 70–80% of the total.

faqs.question: Is 8 people enough for a Halloween party at home?
faqs.answer: Yes. Eight is close to the sweet spot for a flat: everyone fits in one living-room circle, and four pairs clear a scare corner in about 20 minutes. Anything from 6 to 12 works with the room-by-room layout; above 12, the hallway and kitchen jam.

faqs.question: Where should guests put their coats at a small house party?
faqs.answer: On a bed in a room with the main light on and no candles. NFPA reports that 36% of US home candle fires in 2020 to 2024 started in a bedroom, and a pile of coats is exactly the kind of thing that burns.

faqs.question: How do I make a scare corner in a small flat?
faqs.answer: Use the smallest room with a door, never the hallway you leave by. A bedsheet curtain, a phone playing a slow creak and a cold damp glove on a thread are enough for a 4-minute walk-through for two people at a time, lit only by battery tealights.

faqs.question: How loud can a Halloween house party be?
faqs.answer: It depends on your city. In Toronto, amplified music heard inside a neighbour's home must stay under 50 dB(A) from 7 am to 11 pm and under 42 dB(A) after 11 pm, averaged over 10 minutes, with a separate bass limit. Check your own council's rule before the night.

faqs.question: Should I tell my neighbours I'm having a Halloween party?
faqs.answer: Yes, a day ahead, with an end time and your number. A short note under the door saying music drops at 10:45 pm and inviting a text if it gets loud solves most problems before anyone calls a bylaw line.

faqs.question: How long should a small Halloween party at home last?
faqs.answer: Four hours, such as 7 to 11 pm, suits 6 to 12 guests. That fits arrivals, a meal, a 30-minute scare-corner rotation, a debrief circle, one loud music hour and a quiet wind-down before most cities' night limits begin.

faqs.question: Are real candles safe at a Halloween house party?
faqs.answer: Only with rules. NFPA advises keeping candles at least 12 inches (30 cm) from anything that can burn; keep flames to the kitchen counter and one table, name a guest to blow them out at 10:45 pm, and use battery lights everywhere else.

faqs.question: How much does a small Halloween party at home cost per person?
faqs.answer: Our estimate for the layout in this guide is about $11 to $23 a head in US dollars, or $74 to $136 in total for 6 guests and $133 to $237 for 12. Food and drink make up roughly 70% to 80% of that.

faqs.question: What about guests who don't want to be scared?
faqs.answer: Give them a reset room: a door that shuts, a phone charger, water and foam earplugs. The scare corner should be strictly opt-in, two people at a time, and the debrief circle lets non-players join the fun by hearing what happened.

faqs.question: Do I need a permit for a noisy house party?
faqs.answer: Usually not if you stay inside your city's limits. Toronto, for example, offers noise exemption permits for events that would break its bylaw, but a 6 to 12 guest party that turns the music down by 10:45 pm should not need one.

faqs.question: Can a SubhSandesh Halloween page invite all my party guests?
faqs.answer: No. Both SubhSandesh Halloween pages are one-person greeting pages, not party invitations, so use a group chat for the guest list. Keep the page for one person, such as the flatmate or partner who co-hosted.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween House Party Ideas for a Small Flat, Room by Room

The best Halloween house party ideas for a small home start with the floor plan, not the theme: invite 6 to 12 people, give every room one job, keep real flames out of the bedroom where the coats go, and finish before your local quiet hours. In SubhSandesh's Raksha Bandhan 2026 data (n = 89 pages, our nearest festival analogue, not Halloween), 49.4% of pages were built on the day itself, so every step below fits into the day before. And 48.3% of shared SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone, so the neighbour notes here are written to fit one screen.

Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. Below: a room-by-room layout, candle rules from US fire data, one city's real noise limits, a 7 to 11 pm run-of-show and an estimated cost per guest.

## What makes a small Halloween party at home different?

A small Halloween house party is a gathering of roughly 6 to 12 guests in a flat or small house, where the host knows everyone and one conversation can still pull in the whole room. It trades crowd energy for closeness, so it succeeds or fails on layout rather than décor.

The guest count has a basis. Psychologist Robin Dunbar describes friendship networks as cumulative layers of about 5 close friends and 15 best friends, and notes that friendships decay quickly without time invested in them ([Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, March 2025](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11918532)). A 12-person list sits inside that 15-layer, and the same review names laughter, feasting, dancing and emotional storytelling as bonding behaviours a two-bedroom flat can hold in one evening.

## Room-by-room layout for a flat or small house

Give each room one job and say what it is at the door. Each zone lists the same four things: its job, how many it holds at once, its lighting, and our estimated cost (EST, US dollars, our own figures).

### 1. Hallway: the arrival and exit zone

- **Job:** shoes, bags and a printed sign naming every room ("Coats: bedroom. Scares: box room. Reset: study.").
- **Holds:** 2 at a time, because it is also your way out.
- **Lighting:** ordinary bulbs; never fog, cobweb or a blackout curtain on the exit route.
- **EST cost:** $3 for printing and tape.

### 2. Kitchen: all food and drink in one place

- **Job:** every dish and bottle on the counter, so guests drift through instead of crowding a coffee table. One hot pot plus bread feeds 12.
- **Holds:** about 4 standing.
- **Lighting:** full overhead light, since the knives and hot pans live here.
- **EST cost:** $9 to $16 per guest.

### 3. Living room: the debrief circle

- **Job:** sofa plus floor cushions in a loose ring, where each pair leaving the scare corner tells the room the moment that got them.
- **Holds:** all 6 to 12 guests.
- **Lighting:** two lamps with orange or red bulbs, ceiling light off.
- **EST cost:** $10 for two coloured bulbs.

### 4. Box room or study: the scare corner

- **Job:** a 4-minute walk-through for two guests at a time: a bedsheet curtain, a phone under the bed playing a slow creak, a cold damp glove hanging on a thread at face height.
- **Holds:** 2, never more.
- **Lighting:** battery tealights only, because people bump into things in the dark.
- **EST cost:** $12 to $20 for a sheet, gloves and six tealights.

### 5. Bedroom: the coat room

- **Job:** coats on the bed, bags on the floor, door left open.
- **Holds:** storage only; nobody hangs out here.
- **Lighting:** the ceiling light, with no candles and no string lights over the coat pile.
- **EST cost:** nothing beyond what you own.

### 6. Spare corner or balcony: the reset room

- **Job:** a door that shuts, a charging strip, water and foam earplugs, for ten minutes away from scares or volume.
- **Holds:** 2 or 3.
- **Lighting:** whatever lamp is already there.
- **EST cost:** $5 for earplugs.

Why pairs, and why a debrief room? Across five studies at three commercial haunted attractions, feeling more fear and touching other guests strongly predicted people saying the experience brought them closer, yet measured closeness barely moved from before to after ([Emotion, online November 2025](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41264500); abstract only). The authors' interviews suggest talking it over afterwards may be what turns a fright into a bond, which is the living room's whole job.

## Candles and decorations: fire rules for a small space

The US National Fire Protection Association reports that from 2020 to 2024, fire departments attended an estimated [5,894 home fires a year started by candles](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/home-fire-safety/candles), with 63 deaths and 532 injuries a year on average. Over half began when something that burns, such as bedding, curtains, decorations or clothing, sat too close to the flame, and 36% started in a bedroom.

That bedroom figure is why the coat room stays flame-free. NFPA advises keeping candles at least 12 inches (30 cm) from anything that can burn,, a gap a crowded flat loses the moment someone in a cape leans over the table.

- **Two flame zones only:** the kitchen counter and the living-room table. The scare corner and hallway get battery lights.
- **Tape the 30 cm circle.** Measure once with a ruler and mark it on the table, so nobody parks a paper bat inside it.
- **Name a flame keeper.** One guest who blows out every candle at 10:45 pm and whenever a room empties; NFPA counts 21% of candle fires as left unattended, discarded or misused.
- **Seat capes away from flames.** Wide sleeves, tulle and wigs pass closer to a table candle than décor does.

## Noise and neighbours: one city's real rule

Quiet hours are local, so check your own council. As one worked example, the City of Toronto's noise page (updated 18 September 2026) says [amplified music heard inside a neighbour's home must stay under 50 dB(A) from 7 am to 11 pm and under 42 dB(A) from 11 pm to 7 am](https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/public-notices-bylaws/bylaw-enforcement/noise/), averaged over 10 minutes. It sets a separate bass-weighted limit of 65 dB(C) by day and 57 dB(C) at night, and sends parties spilling onto the street to the police non-emergency line rather than bylaw officers.

That limit is the same on a Saturday and a Sunday, so the 2026 and 2027 plans match: music down by 10:45 pm. Bass carries through shared walls more than voices, so cut the bass first and put the speaker against an outside wall.

Slip a note under the neighbours' doors a day ahead. Two phone-length versions:

> - "Hi, it's Asha from flat 4. Ten friends are over for Halloween on Saturday from 7 pm. Music goes down at 10:45 and we're done by 11. Too loud? Text me on [number] and I'll fix it within five minutes."
> - "Halloween drinks at ours on the 31st, 7 to 11 pm. You're welcome to drop by, and if it gets noisy, knock and we'll turn it down."

## A 4-hour Halloween run-of-show, 7 pm to 11 pm

Four hours suits 6 to 12 guests because the meal, the scare corner and the one loud hour each need 30 to 60 minutes. The timings assume 12 guests, or six pairs; for Sunday 31 October 2027, start an hour earlier if guests work on Monday.

- **6:15 pm:** light the kitchen and table candles only, check the taped circles, clear the hallway.
- **7:00 pm:** arrivals; the hallway sign does the house tour.
- **7:30 pm:** kitchen opens; guests eat standing or on cushions.
- **8:15 pm:** scare corner opens. Six pairs at 4 minutes each, plus a minute to reset, takes 30 minutes.
- **8:50 pm:** debrief circle, two minutes per pair.
- **9:30 pm:** music up, the only loud hour.
- **10:30 pm:** music down, bass off.
- **10:45 pm:** the flame keeper puts out every candle; dessert and tea.
- **11:00 pm:** goodbyes inside the flat, not on the stairs, then text the neighbour that you're done.

## What a small Halloween house party costs per guest

The table compares three guest counts using our own US-dollar estimates for the layout above; prices vary by city, so treat them as a starting point.

| Guests | Food and drink (EST) | Lighting, décor and batteries (EST) | Total and per head (EST) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | $54–96 | $20–40 | $74–136, about $12–23 each |
| 9 | $81–144 | $20–40 | $101–184, about $11–20 each |
| 12 | $108–192 | $25–45 | $133–237, about $11–20 each |

Per head, the cost flattens above 9 guests because the scare corner and lamps are a one-off spend. Food is roughly 70% to 80% of every row, so one hot pot is where the saving lies.

## SubhSandesh's Halloween pages: for one person, not the party

Neither SubhSandesh page is a party tool: they will not invite a crowd or collect RSVPs. Each is a one-person greeting page with partner, bestie, family and kids modes, best kept for the person who made the night possible, such as the flatmate who gave up their bed to the coats.

The [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) suits a quick thank-you: they knock three times, carve a pumpkin until your word glows and read your letter by flashlight, with up to six photos and about 5 minutes to make. The [cinematic premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) suits a bigger gesture: a voice note up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos, a reply box, and an optional unlock time you can set for 11 pm so it opens as the last guest leaves, in about 10 minutes.

Both take an optional password, and 38.5% of SubhSandesh creators set one before sharing (2,000 of 5,199). If your co-host cares more about music than Halloween, a [radio-show dedication page](https://subhsandesh.in/dedication) lets them hear your voice introduce their song. Skip all of this in three cases:

- **More than 12 guests, or a light sleeper behind a shared wall:** book a table somewhere instead.
- **Your co-host does not read English:** both pages' interface is English only.
- **They are beside you at 11 pm:** say it out loud; a link adds nothing.

## Sources

- Dunbar, "Why friendship and loneliness affect our health," *Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences*, 6 March 2025. [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC11918532)
- Wiley et al., "Haunted attraction," *Emotion*, 20 November 2025, abstract only. [Europe PMC](https://europepmc.org/article/MED/41264500)
- National Fire Protection Association, "Safety with candles," 2020–2024 statistics, undated. [nfpa.org](https://www.nfpa.org/education-and-research/home-fire-safety/candles)
- City of Toronto, "Noise," updated 18 September 2026. [toronto.ca](https://www.toronto.ca/city-government/public-notices-bylaws/bylaw-enforcement/noise/)
